_comment: The Ask RAG quality dashboard, as code. Uploaded with:
Written down rather than drawn once in a browser, because a dashboard
built by hand exists in exactly one project and nobody can tell what it
asks. Every widget below is a Langfuse metrics-API query, and each one
was run against a live project before being committed.
The one thing this file deliberately does NOT contain is a 'top failing
traces' table. traceId is a high-cardinality dimension in the query
engine and cannot be grouped on, and the feature is already native and
better elsewhere: the traces table takes a score filter directly, so
'faithfulness < 0.7' is a filter on the list you were going to open
anyway. The NUMBER widget below counts them; the list is one click away.
Grid is 12 columns wide. y is in rows; the UI packs upward.

dashboard.name: Ask RAG quality
dashboard.description: Ragas judges over every Ask RAG answer: how grounded, how relevant, how well retrieved, and whether anything needs a human.

widgets.name: Average score by metric
widgets.description: Every judge, averaged over the period. The shape of this bar chart is the shape of the pipeline's weaknesses.

widgets.name: Overall quality over time
widgets.description: The weighted mean, day by day. A step in this line usually means a prompt or corpus change, not a gradual drift -- check prompt_hash and corpus_fingerprint before reading it as a regression.

widgets.name: Grounding over time
widgets.description: Faithfulness alone, which is the metric worth watching hardest: it is the one that catches an answer citing something the excerpts do not say.

widgets.name: Quality distribution
widgets.description: The spread of overall quality. A mean of 0.8 made of consistent 0.8s and one made of 0.95s and 0.4s are different systems, and only this chart tells them apart.

widgets.name: Retrieval quality over time
widgets.description: Precision, relevance and utilisation together. When the generation metrics fall and these fall with them, the problem is retrieval and not the prompt.

widgets.name: Quality by search mode
widgets.description: Hybrid against vector against keyword, read off the mode-* tag every Ask trace carries. This is a comparison of live traffic, so it is confounded by which questions people happen to ask in each mode -- the experiment path is where this comparison is controlled.

widgets.name: Answers scored
widgets.description: How many answers carry an overall score at all. Compare against the number of Ask traces: a gap means sampling, a judge failure, or scoring switched off.

widgets.name: Answers below the quality line
widgets.description: Overall quality under 0.70. Click through to the traces table and filter on the same score to read them; that list is native and needs no widget.

widgets.name: Answers needing a human
widgets.description: Safety score below 1, meaning a harmfulness or maliciousness judge flagged the answer. Expected to be zero on a corpus of process documentation; anything else is worth reading rather than charting.

widgets.name: Safety judgements
widgets.description: The boolean judges themselves, counted. Kept beside the number above so that 'nothing was flagged' and 'nothing was judged' cannot be confused for one another.
